title: Towing Company Funding
seo_title: Towing Company Funding: Trucks & Cash Flow | Fidelity Funding
meta_description: Towing company funding for wreckers and flatbeds, insurance and slow motor club payments. Learn options for 24/7 tow operators and small fleets.
dek: Trucks cost six figures, insurance is steep, and motor clubs pay weeks later. Funding helps tow operators add trucks and cover the gap.
intro: It is 2 a.m., a call comes in, and your only flatbed has a failed hydraulic line. You can turn down the job, or you can find a repair shop and a way to pay for it before dawn. Tow operators live in this reality: the equipment that earns the money is also the most likely to break at the worst possible time.

Towing combines heavy equipment, round-the-clock labor and an unusual payer mix. Some revenue is immediate, such as private-pay and cash calls, while some arrives by invoice from motor clubs, insurance companies, municipalities and dealers. Police rotation calls, accident scenes and impound work come with their own paperwork and timelines.
This page explains how cash flows through a towing company and how owners use outside funding for trucks, repairs and the payment gap.

sections.h2: Trucks, insurance and the cost of being ready
paragraphs: A light-duty flatbed, a wrecker or a heavy-duty rotator represents a major investment, and insurance for towing, garage-keepers coverage and on-hook liability can be expensive. Every truck also needs fuel, tires, maintenance, DOT compliance and a licensed, insured driver.
You pay for being available even when the phone is quiet. A truck parked on a slow night still carries insurance, a payment and a driver on call.

sections.h2: Motor club and insurer payment timing
paragraphs: Roadside assistance and insurance referral work commonly pays on invoice, and payment can take weeks, with deductions or disputed charges slowing it further. Municipal and police-rotation work also follows its own billing cycle.

Meanwhile, drivers and fuel must be paid now. Operators with a high share of invoiced work often feel the squeeze first. Tracking receivables by payer shows which accounts cost you most in waiting time.

A new truck should earn its payment. Before buying, estimate the extra calls you can actually take, whether you need another driver, and how quickly the truck would be utilized. A second truck with no extra demand simply doubles your fixed cost.

Commercial vehicle financing typically spreads the purchase across a term and uses the truck as security. Used trucks cost less but may bring repair risk; budget for it. For urgent repair needs, faster working capital may be better suited.

Suppose you want to add a $95,000 flatbed that could handle about 90 extra calls a month at an average of $140, or roughly $12,600 in revenue. After driver pay, fuel and maintenance, assume it nets $4,500 a month. A hypothetical vehicle financing offer of $95,000 over 60 months with total repayment near $118,000 comes to about $1,970 a month.

That leaves room in the net. A hypothetical short advance for the full price at a 1.25 factor rate would mean $118,750 total payback over a short period, which would likely exceed the truck's monthly net. For a separate $8,000 emergency repair, though, a quick advance could keep a working truck earning. A tow-truck advance carries terms set by the funding partner and its underwriting.

Funding partners typically look at deposits, time in business and the stability of your cash flow. Tow operators can help their case by showing call volume trends, a list of payers, and proof of insurance and licensing. If you accept card payments at the scene, the processing side matters too. Fidelity's card-processing partner, PayPilot by MCCPS, offers statement review and competitive pricing, with modern terminals and POS integration for mobile payments.
Rules on towing rates, storage fees and consent vary by state and municipality, so confirm compliance with local authorities and advisors.
steps: List receivables by payer with age and typical days to pay.
Estimate the added calls and net income of any new truck.
Separate repair needs from growth purchases.
Gather insurance, licensing and recent bank statements.
Compare vehicle financing and working capital by total payback.

paragraphs: Fidelity Funding is a broker. You complete a short application, we run a soft credit pull for the initial review, and a specialist reviews options from our funding partners with you. Towing operators often hear back within hours and see money within 24 hours of approval, though timing can vary. If a truck is down right now, say so. Begin the application for your towing company when you are ready.

Keep every tow ticket, authorization and photo organized so invoices go out quickly and disputes are rare. Follow up on invoices at fixed intervals, and track which payers deduct fees or reject claims. Faster billing is often the cheapest funding you can find. Ask about electronic payment options and be careful about accepting terms that stretch beyond your cash cushion.

key_takeaways: Tow trucks are expensive to own and costly to have down.
Motor club and insurer invoices create a gap between work and payment.
A new truck should be justified by real extra call volume.
Vehicle financing often suits trucks, while faster funding suits urgent repairs.

faq.q: Can I finance a tow truck or flatbed?
faq.a: Often yes through commercial vehicle financing, which uses the truck as part of the security. Down payment, credit and time in business matter, and approval and terms vary by funding partner and underwriting. Your specialist can set truck financing beside faster funding options for your towing company.

faq.q: Can funding help with slow motor club payments?
faq.a: Many operators use working capital or a line of credit to bridge payroll and fuel while invoices are outstanding. Invoice-based options may also be discussed. What a towing company can access depends on its finances and the underwriting review. Bring your payer list and aging report. Applying for tow-truck funding does not oblige you to take whatever offer comes back.

faq.q: Can I get money quickly for a repair?
faq.a: Decisions often come within hours and funding often within 24 hours once approved, but timing varies. Compare the cost of the funds to the revenue the truck earns while running. Repair quotes and insurance documents help the review. Read any towing equipment agreement closely and ask about every clause that is unclear.

Newer companies may have fewer options, and some funding partners require minimum time in business. A specialist can tell you what may be available. Share how long you have been operating and your truck count. Of all the paperwork a towing company can provide, recent bank statements are usually the most useful.
